turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on he, she and it with -s?
turns.tutor:
Sure. Let me think aloud with an example: "Ali ___ (read) books."
Step 1: Who? Ali. Ali is a "he".
Step 2: After he, she or it, the verb needs -s. So "read" becomes "reads".
Result: "Ali reads books."
Rule: after he, she or it, add -s (or -es) to the verb.
Right: "She cooks rice." Wrong: "She cook rice."
Your turn. Write the correct form: My sister ___ (play) tennis on Sundays. (answer with only the verb)
